description.en: Sanjaks of Beirut (incl. Tyre/Sur district in southern Lebanon), Acre (Galilee; northern border Ras al-Naqura to Lake Hula) and Nablus (from the Jezreel valley to north of Jaffa, east to the Jordan).
description.ar: سناجق بيروت (بما فيها منطقة صور في جنوب لبنان)، وعكا (الجليل؛ حدودها الشمالية من رأس الناقورة إلى بحيرة الحولة)، ونابلس (من مرج ابن عامر إلى شمال يافا، وشرقًا حتى الأردن).
description.he: סנג׳קים של ביירות (כולל מחוז צור בדרום לבנון), עכו (הגליל; הגבול הצפוני מראס א-נקורה ועד אגם החולה) ושכם/נאבלוס (מעמק יזרעאל ועד צפון יפו, ומזרחה עד הירדן).

sources.locator: section 'Administrative Reorganization after the Enactment of the 1864 Vilayet Law'
sources.quote: The latter included (in addition to the Sanjaqs of Tripoli and Lattakieh) the Sanjaqs of Beirut, Acre and Nablus.
Balqa (a subdistrict within the Sanjaq of Nablus to the east of the Jordan River) was appended to the Province of Syria.
The Sanjaq of Acre was bordered to the north by the Qada (subdistrict) of Sur (Tyre) in the Sanjaq of Beirut, which covered Southern Lebanon.
after which it was attached to the province of Sidon, and then to the province of Beirut in 1887/1888.
The corresponding western half, still excluding Lebanon and also the sanjaq of Jerusalem, was called the vilayet of Beirut.
A peculiarity of this vilayet was that its northern portion was divided from its southern portion by the intervening province of Lebanon
Palestine lay, administratively speaking, partly in the autonomous Sanjaq (Liwa, Mutesarriflik) of Jerusalem, partly in the Vilayet of Beirut.
